object_description: three offset buildings of different proportions with a front building towards the main street
design_condition: three staggered buildings of different proportions respond each to the specific city character that surrounds them, with an articulated front building set back slightly from the main street

positive: A composition of three offset buildings starts an urban reinterpretation of the area
Its physiognomy can react to the specific counterparts of old town and suburb
The three buildings respond with different proportions to the city characters around them
The front building mediates spatially between the upper and lower streets in an orthogonal form
The two adjoining buildings respond to the preserved suburban row and to the loose hillside structure
The arrangement of the auditorium and foyer along the street promotes public perception of the university
These areas are architecturally distinguished with a slight arcade design
Placing all large rooms on the ground floor gives easy accessibility for large flows of people
On the upper floors three inner courtyards divide the plans into easily lit usable areas
The wings are reached from a central hall also intended as a spacious lounge and learning area
The different positioning of the courtyards creates different spatial situations for varied usage scenarios
The roof garden crown with covered walkway can support the desired beacon character
The clearly structured design and compact form promise construction costs in the medium range
The self-confident urban development of the campus as head of a new district is a convincing idea
negative: The expected spacious forecourt breaks down into a tightly structured staircase landscape
The small-scale entrance area cannot correspond to the habitus of the urban order sought
The staircase and terrace landscape creates an unsightly appearance of a lowering of the building
This affects the adjacent usable spaces and creates unattractive views
The arcade design is not yet resolved in the integration of the ground floor
It lacks a necessary response to the high noise level along the street
Individual rooms and functional areas on the ground floor receive poor lighting or none at all
Vertical access and service areas at the interfaces severely limit flexibility across the plan
Whether the student bar is a suitable use for the roof crown is questioned
Significant optimisation would be necessary to achieve the desired sustainability certification
The uniform facade language equalises the distinctions made in the building structure
It makes a specific architectural expression for the campus more difficult
Dealing with the topography leads to tectonic and operational divisions that obscure the initial idea
